stories.headline: Accenture spends $4.18B on Dragos majority stake plus runZero and NetRise to push into OT security

key_facts.fact: Accenture announced Thursday it will take a majority stake in Dragos and fully acquire runZero and NetRise at a combined enterprise value of approximately $4.175 billion.

The Dragos majority stake is valued at $3.25 billion; the deal builds on Accenture's existing $10 billion cybersecurity business and the targets together generate $208 million in annual recurring revenue.

Dragos is an OT threat-detection specialist; runZero (founded by Metasploit creator HD Moore) handles asset discovery and attack-surface intelligence; NetRise focuses on firmware-level visibility and software supply chain security.
The transactions are expected to close in August or September 2026; Dragos CEO Robert M. Lee will continue leading the combined business.
Accenture shares fell over 11% in premarket trading as the company cut its FY revenue growth forecast top end to 3–4% (from 3–5%), signaling weak discretionary IT consulting spend.

stories.headline: Amazon in talks to sell Trainium AI chips for use in third-party data centers

key_facts.fact: Amazon's senior vice president overseeing semiconductor, AI and quantum, Peter DeSantis, said AWS is in talks to sell its Trainium AI chips for use in other companies' data centers — chips previously exclusive to AWS.
DeSantis said a key driver is rising international demand — particularly in Europe — for locally controlled, sovereign AI infrastructure.
DeSantis dismissed concerns the external sales would cannibalize AWS cloud revenue, citing 'so much underconsumption in AI.'

CEO Andy Jassy estimated in April that selling Amazon's chips at run-rate to AWS and outside customers could push the chip business toward ~$50B in annualized revenue, up from a current ~$20B run rate across Trainium, Graviton and Nitro.
Trainium-line revenue commitments exceed $225 billion as of April, and Trainium4 is already booked more than a year ahead of shipment.
The move mirrors a similar shift by Google, which has begun selling its custom TPUs to select external data centers.

stories.headline: Amazon in talks to sell Trainium AI chips outside AWS, taking direct aim at Nvidia

key_facts.fact: Amazon's AI chief Peter DeSantis told Bloomberg from Paris that AWS is in talks to sell its Trainium AI chips for use in third-party data centers; DeSantis declined to name potential customers.

Rising international demand for sovereign AI infrastructure, particularly in Europe, is a major driver behind the push; DeSantis said AWS sees how businesses build AI infrastructure as 'on the cusp of rapid, wide-ranging change.'

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy in his April shareholder letter said the company's chip business could be a ~$50 billion annual run rate if sold to third parties; current Trainium3 capacity is largely sold out, and the Trainium chip line has generated more than $225 billion in revenue commitments.

Trainium chips are already used through AWS by customers including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Uber; production constraint at TSMC, which has supplanted Apple as the foundry's largest customer, is a key bottleneck for broader sales.

Nvidia is currently on a $326 billion revenue run rate; a $50 billion Amazon chip business would be akin to Intel's annual revenue and represent one of the more material challenges to Nvidia's AI chip dominance.

stories.headline: About 200 Glasswing firms keep Mythos Preview access despite US shutdown order

key_facts.fact: Roughly 200 organizations enrolled in Anthropic's Project Glasswing program have preserved access to Mythos Preview after a US government order forced the broader public Mythos rollout to be shut down.
Cybersecurity firms Dragos and Cisco Systems confirmed to Bloomberg they have retained access to Mythos Preview through Glasswing.
European cybersecurity agency ENISA, invited to join Glasswing before the US block, was told its planned access would be revoked.
Glasswing partners use Mythos Preview to scan codebases for vulnerabilities; the model has surfaced more than 10,000 high- or critical-severity flaws across participating organizations.
Anthropic is committing up to $100M in Mythos Preview usage credits to Glasswing participants, with model pricing of $25/$125 per 1M input/output tokens for paid use after the preview.
Anthropic's relationship with the US government ruptured this year after it refused to allow military use of its models for domestic surveillance or fully autonomous weapons systems.

stories.headline: Apple opens iOS to alternative app marketplaces and external payments in Brazil under CADE deal

key_facts.fact: Apple announced on June 18 that iOS developers in Brazil can distribute apps through alternative marketplaces and process payments outside Apple's In-App Purchase, as part of a settlement with Brazilian competition regulator CADE.
Apps distributed outside the App Store will pay a 5% Core Technology Commission on digital goods and services; alternative marketplaces must be authorized by Apple.

Inside the App Store, the standard commission on digital goods drops to a maximum of 21% (from up to 30%), with a reduced 10% rate for Small Business Program, Video Partner Program, and subscriptions after their first year; in-app purchase adds a 5% processing fee.
Developers who direct users to an external website will pay a 15% Store Services Commission for purchases completed within seven days of an external purchase link tap.
The changes ship on iOS 26.5 and later; current Apple Developer Program members must agree to the updated license terms by July 6, 2026.
The CADE dispute originated from a 2022 complaint by Latin American e-commerce giant MercadoLibre.

stories.headline: US Commerce Sec Lutnick tells ASML he suspects a top EUV chip tool may have reached China

key_facts.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told ASML senior leaders in a series of recent meetings that he's concerned one of the Dutch company's EUV lithography machines may have made it into China in violation of US-led export restrictions.
ASML has never been allowed to ship EUV systems to China due to curbs imposed under the first Trump administration; EUV machines are required by TSMC to manufacture processors for Nvidia and Apple.

ASML created and circulated a document in Washington titled 'No indication of any ASML EUV System in China' after the April meeting with Lutnick; it states there are 314 EUV machines in operation worldwide, 26 decommissioned, and none in China.

Senior administration officials told Bloomberg they have evidence ASML shipped specialty equipment used to transport EUV machines as well as other components, but said the proof is too sensitive to disclose.

A bipartisan bill moving through Congress would go further and ban all of ASML's deep ultraviolet (DUV) shipments to China; DUV accounts for roughly 20% of ASML's expected 2026 revenue. The bill cleared a key committee in April.

ASML says EUV machines are the size of a school bus, weigh 180 tons, and that customers 'cannot remove, transport and relocate EUV systems without ASML involvement due to specialised handling procedures.'

stories.headline: US Commerce Secretary Lutnick tells ASML one of its EUV machines may be in China; ASML denies

key_facts.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told ASML's senior leaders in a series of recent meetings that one of its top-of-the-line EUV lithography machines may have made its way into China in violation of US-led export restrictions.
ASML has never been allowed to ship EUV systems to China because of curbs imposed during the first Trump administration; EUV is used by TSMC to manufacture processors for Nvidia and Apple.
ASML denies the claim, saying the tools are the size of a school bus, manufactured in limited quantities, and require constant upkeep from ASML employees — and that no EUV machine is in China.

Senior US officials say they have evidence ASML shipped EUV-related components and transport equipment to China but have repeatedly declined to share it with Bloomberg or ASML; ASML circulated a document in Washington in April titled 'No indication of any ASML EUV System in China'.

A bipartisan US bill (MATCH Act) introduced in April 2026 would ban all ASML DUV shipments to China, going beyond the existing EUV ban; DUV currently accounts for roughly a fifth of ASML's expected 2026 revenue, and China's share of system sales fell from 36% to 19% in Q1 2026 due to stricter controls.

stories.headline: Ex-White House AI adviser Dean Ball joins OpenAI to lead new Strategic Futures team

key_facts.fact: Dean Ball, former Senior Policy Adviser for AI and Emerging Technology in the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, will join OpenAI on July 6 as head of a new team called Strategic Futures.

Strategic Futures will report to Chief Strategy Officer Jason Kwon and span both public-facing policy proposals and OpenAI's internal governance, working with the Preparedness, legal, policy, National Security and Global Affairs teams.
The team's mandate explicitly covers catastrophic risk, recursive self-improvement, labor market impact and the relationship between frontier labs and government.
Ball co-authored the White House AI Action Plan released last summer and previously was a senior fellow at the Foundation for American Innovation — a role he will retain on a non-resident basis.

Ball has publicly criticized the Trump administration's actions against Anthropic, including the Pentagon's designation of the company as a supply-chain risk and the White House's export limits on Anthropic's Fable model.
The hire follows OpenAI's recent recruitment of Noam Shazeer from Google to lead architecture research.

organizations: White House Office of Science and Technology Policy

stories.headline: General Intuition in talks to raise $300M at ~$2B from Bezos, Schmidt for spatial-AI agents

key_facts.fact: New York-based General Intuition is in talks to raise around $300 million at a valuation of just over $2 billion to train AI agents in spatial-temporal reasoning.
Backers in the new round include Jeff Bezos and Eric Schmidt, plus existing investors Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst.
The round comes only eight months after the company's $134M seed and quadruples its valuation; total funding will exceed $400M in under a year.

The startup trains embodied AI and world models on roughly 2 billion video game clips per year from Medal's 10 million monthly active users — first-person, interactive footage rather than spectator-perspective gameplay.
General Intuition rejected a reported ~$500M acquisition offer from OpenAI before pursuing the raise.
The capital will scale compute capacity to ship a new product by late summer or early fall.

stories.headline: Zhipu's GLM-5.2 tops Artificial Analysis as leading open-weights model with score of 51

key_facts.fact: GLM-5.2 scores 51 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1, the highest among open-weights models and ahead of MiniMax-M3 (44), DeepSeek V4 Pro max (44) and Kimi K2.6 (43).
Among frontier models overall, GLM-5.2 (51) trails only Fable 5 (60), Opus 4.8 (56) and GPT-5.5 (55) on the index — placing it on the Pareto frontier of intelligence vs cost per task.
The model retains the GLM-5.1 architecture footprint at 744B total parameters with 40B active per inference, but expands the context window from 200K to 1M tokens.

Capability gains concentrate in scientific reasoning: CritPt +16 points to 21%, Humanity's Last Exam +12 points to 40%, SciCode +7 points to 50%; GDPval-AA v2 reaches 1524 versus 1514 for proprietary GPT-5.5.
On FrontierSWE, a long-horizon coding benchmark, GLM-5.2 trails Opus 4.8 by 1% while edging past GPT-5.5 by 1% and Opus 4.7 by 11%.
GLM-5.2 is priced at $1.4/$4.4/$0.26 per 1M input/output/cache-hit tokens on Zhipu's first-party API and is released under an MIT license with weights on HuggingFace and ModelScope.

stories.headline: Google guarantees $3.2B to fund NY data center that will rent its TPUs to Anthropic

key_facts.fact: Google provided a $3.2 billion financial guarantee to fund a New York data center that will rent its tensor processing units (TPUs) to Anthropic, mirroring Nvidia's playbook of underwriting customer demand for its chips.

Google plans to sell TPUs more directly to outside customers and has rolled out a new chip; some clients are seeing up to 30% cost savings and 4x performance versus alternatives, with Google planning to raise $85 billion for more AI infrastructure.

Anthropic earlier disclosed an April 2026 deal with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity starting in 2027; Claude's run-rate revenue reached $30 billion in 2026, up from about $9 billion at end of 2025, with 1,000+ business customers each spending over $1 million annually.

Google has previously contracted to sell three million TPUs to Intel for production beginning in 2028 and is in talks with Samsung for its next-gen 'Icefish' 10th-gen TPU and Axion processors, signaling a broader push to diversify foundry sourcing as it scales its custom-silicon business.

stories.headline: India's Telegram ban triggers 49% VPN download spike; Delhi High Court upholds restriction

key_facts.fact: Tuesday June 16 marked the biggest VPN-app download day in India since at least the start of 2025; downloads of major VPN apps rose 49% from a daily average of 139,000 to 208,000, per Appfigures.
Proton VPN downloads on Apple's App Store rose 113%, Turbo VPN rose 85%, NordVPN App Store downloads rose 41%, ExpressVPN on Google Play rose 31%.
Proton said daily registrations from India rose 120% above baseline on Wednesday, after hourly registrations spiked 150% on Tuesday evening following the restriction.

India's Ministry of Electronics and IT issued the order under Section 69A of the IT Act, delisting Telegram from Indian storefronts until June 22 and separately directing Telegram to disable its message-editing feature in India until June 30.
Telegram challenged the order in the Delhi High Court, arguing authorities should target specific content rather than block the entire platform; the court upheld the restriction on Friday.

The restriction was tied to the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET-UG) re-test, with the National Testing Agency flagging Telegram channels like 'PAPER LEAKED NEET' and 'Re-Neet 2026' allegedly soliciting payment for purported exam material.
The X account of Proton VPN GM David Peterson was withheld in India after he posted about the surge in signups.

organizations: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

stories.headline: Intel hires former SK Hynix CEO Seok-Hee Lee as EVP to lead Intel Foundry advanced packaging

key_facts.fact: Intel announced on June 18 the appointment of Seok-Hee Lee as executive vice president of Intel Foundry, reporting directly to CEO Lip-Bu Tan, to lead advanced packaging, system integration, back-end technology development, and back-end manufacturing.

Lee will scale advanced packaging technologies into high-volume manufacturing, including EMIB-T (Intel's 2.5D packaging) and High-Density Hybrid Bonding (HBI), a next-generation 3D packaging process; Navid Shahriari, who had been responsible for packaging, will retire.

Lee was CEO of SK Hynix from December 2018 through 2022, where he drove development of high-bandwidth memory critical to AI; he then served as president and CEO of SK On (battery) until May 2026, and previously spent about a decade at Intel beginning in 2000 leading 32-nanometer transistor development.

Under the new structure, Naga Chandrasekaran continues as EVP of Intel Foundry focused on front-end technology development and manufacturing, including accelerating the ramp of Intel 18A and 14A nodes.
Intel shares jumped 9% premarket Wednesday after Trump said Apple agreed to work with Intel on US chip design and manufacturing; the Lee hire was Intel's first major leadership move since.

stories.headline: Reliance's Jio Platforms files DRHP for India IPO valued by analysts at $130–180B

key_facts.fact: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani announced at the company's 49th AGM on June 19 that Jio Platforms' board approved the draft red herring prospectus, which will be filed with SEBI the same day.
The IPO will be a fresh issue of up to 27 crore (270 million) equity shares of face value Rs 10 each; the issue price will be set through a book-building process.
Analysts estimate the Jio IPO could be India's biggest public offering ever, with a valuation of $130–180 billion.
RIL currently holds 66.43% of Jio Platforms, with Meta and Google holding significant portions of the remainder.
Ambani said the IPO process is being led by his children Akash, Isha and Anant, and called the Jio listing the company's most significant value-creation event of the year.

stories.headline: Meta contracts ~1.6 GW of AI compute from Crusoe across Texas and Missouri data centers

key_facts.fact: Meta is under contract to buy AI computing capacity from data center developer Crusoe at two sites — Childress, Texas and Warrenton, Missouri — for roughly 1.6 gigawatts combined, according to people familiar.

Neither the dollar value nor the delivery timeline was disclosed; spokespeople for Meta and Crusoe declined to comment. A single gigawatt is enough to power as many as 750,000 US homes at any given time.

Crusoe, founded in 2018, already has data center deals with Oracle, Microsoft, and Google; earlier this month it said it had contracts for 4.9 GW of capacity, with more than 40 GW in its total project pipeline.
The deal comes after Crusoe was pushed out of development of a major data center in Wyoming after earlier talks with Google fell through, per a prior Bloomberg report.

stories.headline: Samsung Foundry wins talks with AMD, Google, Tesla, Groq as TSMC capacity sells out

key_facts.fact: According to a Nikkei Asia report, a growing list of major chip customers — including AMD, Google, Nvidia-backed Groq, Tesla, and BYD — are in discussions with Samsung Foundry about manufacturing future chips as TSMC's leading-edge capacity is fully booked.
AMD is in talks with Samsung to manufacture certain future CPUs starting in 2028 on Samsung's second-generation 2nm node — its first reported CPU shift to Samsung, with AMD's GPUs remaining at TSMC.
Google is discussing two separate Samsung engagements: next-gen Axion processors around 2028 and components for its 10th-gen TPU codenamed 'Icefish', co-developed with MediaTek.

Tesla has confirmed its next-generation AI6 chip will be produced at Samsung's Texas facility; BYD is in talks with Samsung on 2nm and 4nm autonomous driving SoCs; Groq's LP30 AI inference processor will run on Samsung's 4nm node.

AMD stock rose ~3% and Intel ~4% on June 18 as investors reacted to the Samsung-AMD talks; the TSMC capacity squeeze is also driving overflow to Intel Foundry, with reports that Apple could use Intel's 18A-P process for future M7 production in 2027 and Google ordered 3 million TPUs from Intel for 2028.

stories.headline: SpaceX prepares $20B investment-grade bond sale to refinance xAI-acquisition bridge loan

key_facts.fact: SpaceX bankers are preparing to hold investor calls as early as Monday next week to discuss a bond sale of at least $20 billion — the company's first investment-grade dollar bond issue.

Proceeds will refinance a $20 billion bridge loan taken in February after SpaceX acquired Musk's xAI; the bridge facility matures in September 2027 and accounted for most of SpaceX's $29.1 billion in long-term debt as of March 31.
Bank of America, Citigroup, JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley provided the original bridge and are expected to run the bond deal.
Moody's assigned SpaceX a Baa1 rating on June 18, Fitch gave it BBB+ and S&P assigned BBB — all investment grade.

SpaceX's valuation surged past $2 trillion following last week's Nasdaq debut; the company has a roughly $45 billion compute deal with Anthropic over about the next three years and $4.2B contracted with Alphabet.

stories.headline: US-Iran sign interim MoU ending war; oil falls to pre-war lows as Strait of Hormuz reopens

key_facts.fact: Trump and his Iranian counterpart signed a 14-point memorandum of understanding remotely on Wednesday evening June 17, ahead of an originally planned Friday signing in Switzerland; the deal entered into force with immediate effect.

The agreement covers an immediate end to hostilities (including in Lebanon), reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, lifting of the US naval blockade, and opens a 60-day negotiation period on Iran's nuclear program.
Brent crude futures fell 2.33% to $77.69/barrel on Thursday, while WTI fell 2.46% to $74.90 — Brent's lowest since February 27, the last trading day before the US-Israeli strikes on Iran began.

Under the MoU the US will allow Iran to sell oil and petrochemical products, and the deal requires the US and partners to come up with a $300 billion plan to finance Iran's recovery if Tehran meets nuclear commitments.
VP JD Vance said tankers carrying more than 12 million barrels crossed the Strait of Hormuz overnight Thursday; the deal calls for full traffic capacity to be restored within 30 days.
The MoU defers Iran's nuclear program and missile issues to a 60-day negotiation period; Trump warned the US could 'go right back to dropping bombs' if Iran doesn't comply.

stories.headline: Robotics infrastructure startup XDOF emerges from stealth with $70M and open dataset

key_facts.fact: XDOF emerged from stealth with $70 million in funding to build core infrastructure for robot foundation models, including datasets, robotic systems, and software tools for physical AI.

The round involved Thrive Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, Spark Capital, Lux Capital, and WndrCo; XDOF was co-founded by CEO Philipp Wu, CTO Yide (Fred) Shentu, and COO Nemo Jin and traces its roots to a UC Berkeley teleoperation project called GELLO.

Alongside the raise, XDOF released ABC-130K, which it calls the largest open-source bimanual robot manipulation dataset — over 130,000 demonstrations across 195 tasks, plus 300 hours of simulations and 100 hours of evaluations — developed with researchers from UC Berkeley, Carnegie Mellon, MIT, and Amazon FAR.
XDOF already has roughly 20 active customers, including frontier AI labs, and 60+ employees; it plans to hire a global arm of teleoperators and build proprietary wearable sensors for hand-tracking.
The launch comes weeks after OpenAI announced it's reviving its robotics training program, shut down in 2021, amid broader investor enthusiasm for 'physical AI'.
